_readme: Phase 2 ANSYS calibration harness input. Each entry describes ONE physical design (wall/insulation/geometry) that both our RC-network solver and a real ANSYS thermal run are evaluated against, for the SAME forcing (site + design-day). 'ansys_min_indoor_temp_c' and 'ansys_wall_clock_s' must come from an actual ANSYS run performed by the team -- they are NOT fabricated here. Until real numbers are filled in, 'status' stays 'pending' and engine/validation/ansys_benchmark.py will refuse to compute MAE/speedup for that entry (it will not silently substitute a placeholder). This keeps the same 'no invented numbers' discipline as validate_uvalue.py / validate_transient.py / materials.json's cost_note fields.
_how_to_fill_in: 1) Pick a design below (or add one). 2) Build the equivalent geometry in ANSYS Fluent/Thermal (or ANSYS Workbench Steady-State/Transient Thermal) using the SAME material k/rho/cp from data/materials/materials.json and the SAME hourly forcing (temp/GHI/wind) that engine/validation/ansys_benchmark.py prints for that entry. 3) Run it, record min indoor air temp over the 24h window and wall-clock solve time. 4) Fill ansys_min_indoor_temp_c / ansys_wall_clock_s / status:'complete' below. Only 2-3 runs are required for Phase 2 (calibration only, never inside the live optimizer loop -- see optimizer/surrogate.py docstring).
